member.summary:

AI inside the search itself, as opposed to the text tools a visitor presses a button for.
Three distinct things, each switched on separately because each costs money on a different schedule. Query understanding and re-ranking run during a search, so they are the two that can make a visitor wait - both are bounded by and a search that outruns it is served exactly as it would have been without any of this. The answer card is fetched by the browser after the results are already on screen, so it never delays them.
All off by default. Installing the package must not start spending money at a provider, and these spend it per search rather than per button press.

member.name: P:Imobisoft.Search.Models.AiSearchRules.UnderstandQuery
member.summary:
Reads the query before it runs: corrects the spelling, adds the words the site itself uses for the same thing, and lifts filters and a sort order out of a sentence - so "3 bed houses in Leeds added this month, cheapest first" becomes a term, two filters and a sort.
This is the one that changes what a search finds rather than how it is ordered. Everything it produces is checked against the profile first: a filter it invents that the profile does not define is dropped, and so is a sort option that is not enabled.

member.name: P:Imobisoft.Search.Models.AiSearchRules.Rerank
member.summary:
Re-orders the best matches by how well they actually answer the query, rather than by how many times its words appear. This is the fix for a page that is plainly the right answer and ranks eighth because it says the word once.
Applies to the first page only, and only when the visitor has not chosen a sort order of their own - a "Sort by: newest" dropdown is an instruction, and reordering underneath it would be ignoring it. Best bets stay pinned where the profile pinned them.

Fetched by the browser once the results are rendered, so the page is never held up waiting for it. Cached per term like every other answer, so a popular search is paid for once.

member.name: P:Imobisoft.Search.Models.AiSearchRules.TimeoutMilliseconds
member.summary: How long a search will wait for the stages that run inside it. Past this the search carries on without them: a slow provider must cost a visitor nothing but the AI, and a search that returns late is worse than one that returns unaided.

member.name: P:Imobisoft.Search.Models.AiSearchRules.MaxCallsPerMinute
member.summary:
Calls each stage may make per minute, counted across the whole site.
This is the one that matters most on a public site, and it is not the same thing as the per-visitor limit on the text tools. A visitor presses a button; a search just happens. A crawler walking the search page with a different term every time is not one caller hitting a limit, and a term nobody has searched before cannot come from the cache - so without a ceiling here, how much a site spends is decided by how often it is crawled.
Past the ceiling, searches are served exactly as they would be with this switched off.

The search button for a site header, as a single embeddable component:
@await Component.InvokeAsync("ImobisoftSearchBox")
Closed, it is just a button. Pressing it opens the search bar on the page the visitor is already on - nothing navigates, nothing is fetched.              @await Component.InvokeAsync("ImobisoftSearchBox")

member.name: T:Imobisoft.Search.Web.SearchPageInjectionTagHelperComponent
member.summary:
Renders the whole search page inside one of the site's own pages, without the site writing a line of code.
This is what gets search the site's header, footer and navigation. The package's own route cannot: a layout shares its model with the page inside it, and a site layout declared as @inherits UmbracoViewPage<SomePageViewModel> needs a model that only the site's own controllers can build - from the routed Umbraco page, with its SEO data, its settings and its navigation. Nothing in this package can manufacture one.
So the site renders its own page exactly as it always does - its document type, its controller, its template, its layout - and the search page is placed into it as a block. A tag helper component is how a library adds markup to a view it does not own, which is the same mechanism the header search box already arrives by.
To use it: create a page in Umbraco with whatever document type the site uses for an ordinary content page, then put its path in Search → Settings → Search Page. A site that wants to place search exactly rather than have it placed can render from its own template instead, and this stands aside when it has.
A site that already had a search page before the package needs none of that: the page is recognised by and taken over where it stands, so the links already pointing at it arrive at the package's search. On a page taken over this way the site's own search form and results are stood down too - that is what keeps one search page from showing two searches.
